name: Divisibility and Congruences
description: Gcd, modular arithmetic and the classical theorems built on them.

content.answer: For integers a and b > 0 there are unique q, r with a = bq + r and 0 ≤ r < b.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: gcd(a,b) = ax + by for some integers x, y.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: Repeatedly replace (a,b) with (b, a mod b); the last nonzero remainder is gcd(a,b).

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: a · b (for positive a, b)

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: If a prime p divides ab, then p divides a or p divides b.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: Every integer > 1 factors into primes uniquely up to order.

content.answer: n divides (a - b).

content.answer: gcd(a,n) divides b.

content.answer: gcd(a,n) = 1.

content.answer: If the moduli n1..nk are pairwise coprime, the system x ≡ ai (mod ni) has a unique solution mod n1···nk.

content.answer: If p is prime and p ∤ a, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: If gcd(a,n) = 1, then a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n).

content.answer: The count of integers in 1..n that are coprime to n.

cards.prompt: Euler's criterion for odd prime p

content.answer: a is a quadratic residue mod p iff a^((p-1)/2) ≡ 1 (mod p).

cards.prompt: Which primes are sums of two squares (Fermat)?

content.answer: 2 and the primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4).

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: Every positive integer is a sum of four integer squares.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: Given primes p1..pk, any prime factor of p1···pk + 1 is a new prime.

cards.prompt: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions

content.answer: If gcd(a,d) = 1, then a, a+d, a+2d, ... contains infinitely many primes.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: The number of primes ≤ x is asymptotic to x / ln x.

cards.sourceRef: Niven, Zuckerman & Montgomery, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Wiley)

content.answer: For every n > 1 there is a prime p with n < p < 2n.
